rationale.conceptual: The method uses conventional DFT with Quantum ESPRESSO, but the specific protocol (growing graphene ribbons, extracting flat-to-corrugated transition, computing stress, and simulating stepped terraces with specific cell geometries) requires genuine understanding of the physics and careful implementation. It is an established, multi-part application of DFT, not a simple textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has three main DFT simulation stages (ribbons of varying width, infinite layer, stepped cell) plus scored output extraction. This multi-stage workflow (roughly 4–6 distinct build/run/extract steps) involves setting up QE inputs, iterating over ribbon widths, and post-processing stress tensors. It requires careful orchestration but not extreme length or fragile multi-tool assembly.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper uses standard DFT (Quantum ESPRESSO) to simulate graphene on Ni(100) surfaces, extracting critical ribbon width, stress thresholds, and a terrace-width ratio. The method requires careful translation of physical insight into simulation protocols (building slab models, fixing edges, relaxing structures, and computing stress). While the individual computations are well-established, the custom multi-part workflow (ribbon series, infinite layer, stepped cell) and the need to interpret corrugation and stress make it a non-trivial but not research-novel implementation task. The execution consists of three main DFT phases plus output extraction, with moderate tooling dependencies.
